# Subrole Filler Roll-up Reference

Complete reference for the `glassfrog subrole-actors` command — the actors filling a role's **direct sub-roles**, rolled up one level.

## Overview

`glassfrog subrole-actors <ROLE_ID>` reads `GET /roles/{role_id}/subroles/actors` and lists the actors filling the anchor role's **direct** sub-roles — one level, not transitive. It is the cross-role counterpart to the actor directory's per-role view: where `glassfrog actors --role-id <id>` surfaces the actors filling **one** role, this rolls up the actors filling that role's direct children. It is the actor-shaped twin of `glassfrog tension subroles`.

The command is its **own** top-level leaf (not `actors subroles …`), and the two-word capability is spelled as a single token — `subrole-actors` — because the return shape is bare actor records (`id`/`name`/`kind`), not the assignment shape of [Role Fillers](role-fillers.md). Paginated — walks every page by default.

Codebase enrichment skipped — not attempted. This reference is based on the interface contracts and the shipped `--help`.

## `glassfrog subrole-actors <ROLE_ID>` — roll up direct sub-roles' fillers

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog subrole-actors <ROLE_ID> [--kind KIND] [--first-page] [--per-page N] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ROLE_ID` | string | required | The **anchor** role whose direct sub-roles' fillers to roll up (`role_…`). Exactly one required; zero or more than one is a usage error, no API call. Not validated locally; the API resolves it. A leaf anchor (no sub-roles) or an unknown/malformed id → `404` (see [Exit codes and errors](#exit-codes-and-errors)). |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | string | — | Filter by actor type, sent as `kind`. **Validated locally** against the closed set `agent`, `human`; an unsupported value is a usage error naming the value and the set, no API call. Sent only when present and non-empty; `--kind ""` behaves as no filter, and is carried on **every** page of the walk. |
| `--first-page` | bool | false | Fetch only the first page and signal if more exist (see [Completeness signalling](#completeness-signalling)). |
| `--per-page` | int | API max | Page size for the walk. The API owns the valid range. |

The endpoint offers no other query filter — there is deliberately no `--role-id` and no `--query` here (those are the actor directory's filters over `/actors`).

### Output

Rendered in the resolved format. Format changes rendering, not fetch depth: the roll-up walks to completion in every format (and `--first-page` limits all formats to one page).

The roll-up reuses the **plural `actors` render key** unchanged — the rows are **bare actor records** (`id`/`name`/`kind`). The assignment fields `focus`/`elected_until` are **not** projected — that is [Role Fillers](role-fillers.md), not this roll-up.

**`full`** — one block per actor:

```
<per_… | agt_…>  [<kind>]
  Name:  <name>
```

**`compact`** — one line per actor:

```
<per_… | agt_…>  [<kind>]  <name>
```

**`json` / `yaml`** — the aggregated `{data:[…]}` document built from each actor's raw bytes (per-page `meta` dropped); a valid empty list is `{"data": []}`, never `null`.

**Empty list** (the sub-roles exist but carry no fillers, or none matched `--kind`): under `full`/`compact`, stdout is the `actors` template's empty line (`no actors`) and the command exits `0`. This `0`-exit empty success is **distinct** from a leaf-anchor `404` failure — the two never conflate.

## Projection fields

### Actor (a roll-up row)

| Field | Human projection | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Id | row lead | `per_…` (person) or `agt_…` (agent); carry it forward into the [Actor read](actors.md). |
| Kind | `[<kind>]` badge | Person vs agent. |
| Name | `Name:` | The actor's name. |

## Completeness signalling

A partial list is never silently presented as complete — signalled via a note on **stderr**.

| Situation | Behaviour | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Default (full walk) | Walks every page and renders the complete set. | 0 |
| `--first-page`, more pages exist | Renders the first page; writes to stderr: `note: more actors exist than shown; re-run without --first-page to fetch all` | 0 |
| Mid-walk failure | Renders actors gathered so far; writes to stderr: `note: result is incomplete — <cause>; the actors shown are a partial set` | non-zero |

## Scope

The roll-up is **one level only**: the command issues exactly one paginated read of the direct sub-roles' actors and makes no attempt to recurse into grand-child roles. A leaf anchor (a role with no sub-roles) surfaces the API's `404` as a normal read failure — no "this role has no sub-roles" interpretation is added.

## Output formats

Inherited persistent root flags, read by cobra inheritance:

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--base-url URL` | Override the API base URL (top rung of the base-URL precedence chain). |
| `-o`, `--output FORMAT` | `full` (default), `compact`, `json`, `yaml`, or a user-template ref. Resolution chain: flag → `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` → `.glassfrogrc output` → `full`. |

The raw API envelope is never emitted under a human format.

## Failure rendering

Failure rendering is **format-aware** (Output-Aware Failure Rendering): under `json`/`yaml` a failure emits the unified error envelope on **stdout**; under `full`/`compact` the diagnostic (cause + next step) goes to **stderr**. The incompleteness notes stay on **stderr** in every format.

## Exit codes and errors

The exit code is the category from the Exit-Code Convention. Every message names the cause and a next step, and never includes the token.

| Condition | Exit | Diagnostic |
|---|---|---|
| Roll-up listed (incl. empty list — sub-roles carry no fillers) | 0 | — (result on stdout; incompleteness note on stderr when applicable) |
| No usable token | 2 | "not authenticated — run `glassfrog auth login` or set GLASSFROG_TOKEN" |
| Unreadable / malformed credential file | 1 | names the credentials file — "fix or re-create it with `glassfrog auth login`" |
| Leaf anchor (no sub-roles) or unknown role id, or other non-2xx (4xx/5xx) | 3 / 4 / 5 | names the HTTP status + extracted detail; per-class next step. No "this role has no sub-roles" interpretation is added — the `404` is surfaced as the shared read failure. |
| Could not reach the wire | 6 | names the transport failure — "check connectivity; the API may be unreachable" |
| 2xx body did not match the expected shape | 3 | "the API response did not match the expected shape — may be an API change; report it" |
| Malformed paging mid-walk | 1 | the walker's text, surfaced inside the incompleteness note |
| Unsupported `--kind` value | 2 | "unsupported --kind value …" + the supported set (`agent, human`); no request sent |
| Base-URL configuration error | 2 | names the malformed base URL + source |
| Invalid `--output` selector | 2 | names the bad format value + the four valid names |
| Wrong positional count (zero / >1) | 2 | cobra's arg-count message; no request sent |

Exit codes by category: `0` success, `1` runtime error, `2` usage error, `3` API error, `4` permission error, `5` rate-limited, `6` network unavailable.
